text: Ysheva Harbor (Japanese: , Isheba-kō) is a landmark in . It is located in the Fonsett Waters of the Leftherian Archipelago, between Fonsett Island and the Isle of Urchon. A Phonex village is located here. Titan ships can sail from here to the Indoline Praetorium.

Wood Gathering (Japanese: , Mokuzai no Shūshū) is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Gormott Province, and is unlocked automatically when Garfont Mercenaries reaches Merc Level 2 and the nation reaches 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 50 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 12 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Ice Mastery", "Transport Mastery" and "Forestry" Field Skills.

Wonderful Stage is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Uraya, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 2 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Production Mastery" and "Beguiling Charms" Field Skills.

Yurem Puffots (Japanese: , Yureimu Shigaru) are enemies in . They are members of the Puffot family, and can be found at level 32-34 at Rigitte Harbor or at level 34-36 on Fonsett Island in the Leftherian Archipelago. Five of them must be defeated to unlock Sever's level 3 Storm Edge, and two of them to unlock Corvin's level 3 Ictus Battle Skill.
Wyn is an NPC in . He is a Gormotti who can be found in the Grodd Residential Zone in Torigoth, Gormott, during Star-Crossed Lovers. He is Carys's husband as well as Nils and Rhiannon's father.

The Wood-Carving Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission The Water City. It enables the purchase of Wood-Carven Queens from the Cmalaf Artwork shop at Torigoth in the Gormott Province.

Yashima Festival is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Leftherian Archipelago, and is unlocked automatically when Garfont Mercenaries reaches Merc Level 4 and the nation reaches 4 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 100 minutes, but it can be reduced down to 25 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Production Mastery", "Fortitude" and "Focus" Field Skills.

World in a Book is a Merc Mission in . It can be received in the Kingdom of Tantal, and is unlocked automatically when the nation reaches 5 stars in Development Level. The time required to complete this mission is 2 hours, but it can be reduced down to 30 minutes by dispatching Blades with the "Info Collector", "Keen Eye" and "Girls' Talk" Field Skills.

This page lists all the quests available in the World Tree. The list may be viewed in the order they become available or the order they appear in the Quest Log. Some quests require certain Blades to be acquired or leveled up. Due to the nature of unlocking Blades, it may be difficult to do all of these quests as soon as the chapter requirement is met. If a quest requires a specific Blade, it will be noted. Terms and abbreviations are explained in the legend at the bottom of the page. |-|Availability Order= This table is divided into sections based on the point in the story at which they become available (if other prerequisites are met). Yrrith is an NPC in . He is a Ardainian sergeant who can be found at Aletta Harbor in the Kingdom of Torna, and is on good terms with one of his troops, MacNeth. He gives the quest Duplicity, upon completion of which his Community is gained. On a later journey to Auresco, he meets someone who bears a resemblance to MacNeth, but upon seeing their face, recognizes them as a Tornan woman. In his frustration, he lashes out at the person, who then becomes teary-eyed. Yrrith vows to find this person again sometime to offer his apology for the "terrible things" he said.

Yesterdale (Japanese: , Bōkyō no Yamafutokoro, Mountain Heart of Nostalgia) is an area in , located in the Cent-Omnia Region. It is the location of the original Colony 9, and is also made up of the remnants of the Cliffs of Morytha.

The Xenoblade Chronicles Special Soundtrack is the official soundtrack album of Xenoblade Chronicles. It was released in Japan on June 10th 2010 as the Xenoblade Special Sound Track (ゼノブレイド スペシャル サウンドトラック). In Europe and Australia, it was released for free on the [http://www.nintendo.co.uk/NOE/en_GB/ European Nintendo Website] as a Stars Reward, on August 19th 2011. Members of the website who registered the game during a certain period of time after its release were able to download the soundtrack for free. The soundtrack consists of twelve songs from the game. They were composed by Yoko Shimomura, Manami Kiyota, Yasunori Mitsuda and ACE+ (Tomori Kudo, CHiCO, and Kenji Hiramatsu). The songs

The XenobladeX Original Soundtrack is an album containing musical tracks from . It was composed by Hiroyuki Sawano and was released through Defstar Records and Sony Music Marketing on May 20, 2015. The soundtrack consists of four CDs and 55 tracks including the Bonus Disc. __TOC__

Zain (Japanese: , Zein) is a High Entia in . He is 142 years old, and resides in Alcamoth with his questing partner, Kurralth. He can be found to the northeast of the Fountain of Eternity in Alcamoth, by the escalator, with Kurralth. After the events at the Mechonis Core, he can be found in Harict Chapel in Valak Mountain. If Adventurers in Peril was not completed, Kurralth (who is in the Chapel) must be spoken to, and he sends the party to find Zain near Three Sage Summit.
Z Power Goggles (Japanese: , Z Pawā Gōguru) are Mechonis goggles in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Zefa Ories (Japanese: , Zegā Oriesu) are enemies in . They are members of the Ories family, and can be found at level 43 just northwest of Nofol Tower on Valak Mountain during the day. Several can be found around Ignia Hill, accompanied by Costa Aries. They can drop the Ories Horns needed for Medical Advancements.

Zeldi Kromars (Japanese: , Zeruti Supikaru) are enemies in . They are members of the Kromar family, and can be found from level 84-87 at the Eryth Sea. Four Zeldi Kromars can be found at Kromar Coast, south of the Soltnar Seal Island, however two of them are in units containing other species of Kromar as well.

Zegia Ories (Japanese: , Zegīa Oriesu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Ories family, and can be found at level 45 on Valak Mountain at night. Several of them can be found around Ignia Hill, accompanied by Hista Aries. They can drop the Ories Horns needed for Medical Advancements.

The Zokhed Pass Shop is a shop in . It is located on Valak Mountain, slightly beyond Zokhed Pass, to the left down the slope. It is manned by a Nopon merchant, and a Nopon nearby gives the party some quests.

Zigs (Japanese: , Jigu) are a type of machine in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are stationary turrets used by the Ganglion, and make up for their lack of mobility with very long detection range. These abilities are hampered during electromagnetic storms.

Zanza's Monado is the third form of the Monado, but since Zanza takes the Monado back during the Mechonis Core events, it is never actually used. With this blade, Zanza is able to control the Bionis itself. He uses this blade to kill Meyneth and take her Monado; however, the power of both Monados combined isn't enough to stop the Monado III.

Ziyse Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts an Orphean Technologies Gatling Gun. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Going Viral. The Ziyse weapons available in-game are: * Storm Ziyse * Soldier Ziyse * Warrior Ziyse * Ophidian Ziyse * Destroyer Ziyse * Striker Ziyse * Delta Ziyse * Original Ziyse * Cosmic Ziyse * Nebulan Ziyse

Zorcyses Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts Orphean Technologies Psycho Launchers. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Good Neighbors. The Zorcyses weapons available in-game are: * Storm Zorcyses * Soldier Zorcyses * Warrior Zorcyses * Ophidian Zorcyses * Destroyer Zorcyses * Striker Zorcyses * Delta Zorcyses * Original Zorcyses * Cosmic Zorcyses * Nebulan Zorcyses
Zaproast Power Bowls are Meat Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Speck Butchers in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Newt.

Zike Ansels (Japanese: , Zaīku Anseru) are enemies in . They are members of the Ansel family and can be found in cloudy weather at level 22-28 in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya, particularly above Farlaine Central Pools at level 22-24 or Fonsa Myma Waters at level 26-28. During petal rain, they do not fly, but can still be found perched on the cliffs to the southeast of Tardy Gate.
Zadazan (Japanese: , Zadazan) is an NPC in . Zadazan is a Nopon who can be found in the Red Room in the Leftherian Archipelago, a secret room hidden underneath Island Base Lindwurm.

The Zekr Marga Quarry (Japanese: , Saisekijō Zekuru Maruga) is a location in . It is a large underground ruin located on the Bionis' Shoulder, beyond the Quarry Colonnade in the Forbidden Hushland. The Marga's Weeping landmark is at the far end of the quarry. Given the enemy layout and presence of Kromar corpses, it seems to be a conflict point between Arachnos and Kromars/Ignas. It must be visited during Stubborn Minds, The Quest for High Ether, and Nonona's Calling. There is a Quiet Moment between Shulk and Nene near the entrance ("Strength in Unity").
Zenze Taos are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Taos family, and can be found at level 89-90 on the Shattered Pathway in The Cavity of Swordmarch.
Ittle Blast (, etal Blast) is one of 's physical s in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected, and a clone of 's . It hits all enemies in a line to inflict , and has a +25% against flying enemies.

AP, short for Art Points, are a mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles and Future Connected. They are used to level up the party's s, which (depending on the Art in question) increases the damage dealt, raises their accuracy, decreases their cooldown, or improves the duration or strength of their additional effects. AP can still be earned after all Arts have been leveled up to the maximum level, even though it can no longer be used. Unspent AP and Art levels are carried over in . Guest party members cannot earn AP. In , AP is not earned during battles.

a prelude to the tragedy is Disc 1, Track 1 on the Xenosaga III: Also Sprach Zarathustra Original Sound Best Tracks album. The melody at 0:07 is used in a memory of a tragedy. The melody at 0:44 is the main melody of mother, I miss you and was used in promised pain and maybe tomorrow~ending medley. It plays in the opening flashback cutscene, when Kevin's mother sends him away from Michtam as it is being destroyed.
Abundant Oceans is a in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It belongs to the Lifesage , and becomes a when reaching rank 15 in this class.

24 Hour Happy People is a short story for Xenoblade Chronicles X written by Kazuho Hyodo, one of the game's scenario writers. The original Japanese text can be found in the [http://xenobladex.jp/24hhp/index.html Special section] of the official website. This story takes place aboard the White Whale as it traveled through space, before it crashlanded on the planet Mira. In this story, Lin goes on an adventure to find quality meat and gets caught up in an underground Skell fighting ring.

The AS0115 Formula XT is a Skell in Xenoblade Chronicles X, temporarily given to Cross during A Girl's Wings so that they can complete the final test of the Skell Flight Module. In the , it cannot have its gear changed or unequipped, and it cannot gain any extra augments. Its insurance is also infinite, meaning that it can always be replaced. Additionally, it cannot be renamed or have its colors changed. However, the armor and weapons can still get augments via L's Shop, but the miranium consumed will be lost forever. Any augments equipped to the Skell will be returned at the end of the mission.

is a track in Xenosaga: The Animation. It is a variation on A Girl's Strength. It plays when Shion uses Queen's Kiss in the Encephalon in Episode 7.
AG-01 is an A.G.W.S. unit in the Xenosaga series. It is commonly seen being used by low ranking officers in the Galaxy Federation Marines' A.G.W.S. squadrons.

100-Series System is a Battle Skill used by and in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition. It adds a probability that advancing a Blade Combo with any will apply a matching element orb, regardless of the combo's level. This skill is identical to the Common Blade skill Orb Master.

The 1st Business District is a sub-area of Fifth Jerusalem in Xenosaga Episode III - Also Sprach Zarathustra. It is business area on the planet containing a Convenience Store, Café Stream, the G.F.G. Showroom, and a park.

Administration Central Area is sub-area of Nortune in Xenogears. It is the seat of power of the Kislev Empire. Kaiser Sigmund's quarters can only be accessed if Rico is in the party.

Albedo is Disc 2, Track 14 on the Xenosaga Original Soundtrack and Disc 2, Track 24 on the album. It plays in the following cutscenes: * Albedo menaces MOMO in the Song of Nephilim while dismembering himself. * Jr. confronts Albedo in the Song of Nephilim. * Jr. almost unleashes his Red Dragon powers against Albedo after the Simeon battle. The track's vocals were sampled for the unused from the music of Xenosaga Episode III.

Affinity Bonuses, or Amulet Bonuses in Future Redeemed, are permanent perks to the party's gameplay capabilities in Xenoblade Chronicles 3 and Future Redeemed. In Xenoblade Chronicles 3, they are obtained via raising Colony Affinity with the Colonies allied to the party (including additional groups such as the Nopon Caravans). Each Colony has five levels of affinity, and raising a given Colony to a specific level of affinity grants a specific Affinity Bonus. In Future Redeemed, Amulet Bonuses are granted via obtaining several s as a reward for completing intermediate steps of Nopon Medals Needed. This is a long-term which entails collecting Nopon Medals from s, containers, and relics, and de
Amazing Stars! is the third skill in 's Cowardice skill branch. It makes his art cooldowns 15% shorter during the night.

Androids are artificial life forms found in the Xenosaga universe. They are typically humanoid or robot-like in appearance and created for the purpose of supporting humans in various tasks. In the present day, Android technology is generally outclassed by Realian technology.
Aphel Aura is a sub-area of in Xenogears. It is the capital city of Shevat.

Ariadne was a planet in the Xenosaga series. It was the home to a research facility, as well as one of the Zohar Emulators. Ariadne disappeared after the failure of a Link Experiment with the Emulator held there.

Ashmed Bapuz is an enemy in Xenosaga Episode II - Jenseits von Gut und Böse. They can cast either Ether Spear or Attacker on themselves to increase their ether/physical power. If ether, they will use Flame Blast and Ether Blast.

is a track in Xenosaga Episode III. It has not been released on any soundtrack or sound selection and not much is known about this track. It plays in the cutscene where T-elos destroys KOS-MOS's core on Rennes-le-Château.
Atalya is a planet in the Xenosaga series. It functions as a common relay point for the U.M.N. Transfer Column to Senir.

Battle Arts, more commonly referred to as simply Arts, are the primary abilities that form characters' movesets in Xenoblade Chronicles and Future Connected. They can be selected during from the Battle Palette, which appears when targeting an enemy. They are mostly offensive moves that deal more than s, but many are instead defensive or supportive in nature. The player selects the lead character's Arts in battle using the D-Pad, while the -controlled party members will automatically use Arts based on factors such as their current , whether they have , and the player's last group command. In addition to their , each party member can learn up to 16 Battle Arts, of which up to 8 can be equipped
Bedside Manner is the second skill in 's Affection skill branch. It increases the power of healing arts she uses by 10%.
Bestest Stars! is the first skill in 's Cowardice skill branch. It increases the he gains from enemies by 20% during the night.

is a track in Xenosaga Episode III. It has not been released on any soundtrack or sound selection and not much is known about this track. It plays as the area music in the Dark Professor's Secret Laboratory on Pedea Island. It also plays during the following cutscenes: * Shion watches Allen's message telling her that the KOS-MOS project is being cancelled. * The Professor and Assistant Scott read over KOS-MOS's basic theory and get to work bringing her back to life with Allen. (The music continues as the area theme on Old Miltia until HaKox is played.) * Shion announces that she'll rest for a bit after playing HaKox while KOS-MOS is being rebuilt.

__NOTOC__ (also translated as ) is Track 6 on the Xenosaga THE ANIMATION Original Soundtrack. It plays in the following scenes: * Cherenkov joins the discussion between Shion and Moriyama regarding KOS-MOS's test data in Episode 1. * The Elsa gates in to hyperspace in Episode 3. * The U-TIC battleship attacks the Elsa in Episode 4. * The party views the doctored footage of the Durandal supposedly attacking Galaxy Federation ships in Episode 7.

It is split into two parts, the first of which plays from the start of the track until 1:21, and the second of which plays from then until the end. The first part plays in the following scenes: * The party enters the Durandal in Episode 5. * The Durandal docks with the Kukai Foundation in Episode 6. The Blackmoon Forest is an area in Xenogears. Fei travels through it after the destruction of Lahan Village.
Bledavik is an area in Xenogears. It is the capital city of the country of Aveh.

Boggle Bomb is a Skell Art in Xenoblade Chronicles X, attached to the B-Bomb series of shoulder-mounted Skell weapons. This Art is often found on Ganglion Skells like the Experimental Composite Qmoeva until the weapons on their backs are destroyed.
Brightest Star is a in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It belongs to the Signifer , and cannot be mastered.

The Briefing Room is an area in Xenosaga: Pied Piper. It is a sub-area in the Galaxy Federation Police Station, situated on its second floor, and serves as the main entry point of the 1875th Special Ops Command into the U.M.N.

is a music track in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It has not been released on any soundtrack or sound selection and not much is known about this track. It plays at the end of the Counterpoint, played in-universe by Boomer on a lute, and accompanied (inaudibly) by Noah and Mio.
Brontes is an enemy in Xenosaga: Pied Piper. This enemy is fought in the training exercise at the virtual version of the Galaxy Federation Police Station.
Carioca is a planet in the Xenosaga series. It is where Vector Industries' First R&D Division Type 1 OS Design Department, a lab integral to several characters' backstories, was located.

Calx II Prototype is an enemy in Xenosaga Episode II - Jenseits von Gut und Böse. He uses Electra, an ice attack, to hit a party member, and can inflict L Heavy to decrease physical attack or L Ether PD to decrease Ether attack. Sometimes when hit, his electricity resistance will increase.
Chapter 18 may refer to: * Chapter 18 (XG) - "City of Peace", the chapter in Xenogears * Chapter 18 (XS1&2) - the chapter in Xenosaga I & II

Citan Uzuki (, Shitan Uzuki), also known as Hyuga Ricdeau (, Hyuga Rikudo), is a playable character in Xenogears. He is a doctor that lives up in the mountains by Lahan Village. Citan knows a little more about the world than most do, and as such he is a mentor figure and friend of Fei.
City Discontent is a discussion in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. Completing it automatically starts the quest Choices.It has optional dialogue depending on whether is in the active party or not.

City Children is a discussion in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It can be obtained after reaching and completing Unsolved Riddle. Discussing it enables (but does not activate) the quest The Kids' Aspiration.
The Coconut Monkey is a minor character in Xenosaga Episode III. He is the Dark Professor's companion who lives on Pedea Island.

The Coalition was the Earth's unified government. Thirty years before the events of Xenoblade Chronicles X, Earth's leaders received word that two alien civilizations, later revealed to be the Samaar Federation and the civilization of the Ghosts, were at war, and that they would attack the planet. In response, the Coalition was formed in order to amass supplies in preparation for the eventual war. The Coalition prepared a project known as the Earthlife Colonization Project, also known as Project Exodus. This project involved developing weapons that would repel the alien forces, and interstellar arks like the White Whale that would help humanity escape and survive should the worst come to pas

Colony Discovered is a track in Future Redeemed. It is used as a jingle for the following instances: * Containers Complete * Relics Complete * Ether Channels Complete * Locations Complete * Landmarks Complete * Secret Areas Complete * Rest Spots Complete * Field Crafting Complete (when completing all of them in an area) * City Survivors Complete * Unique Monster Defeated (excluding Superbosses) * Capture Complete * Intervention Concluded * Fog Rift Sealed * Affinity Scene Viewed * Community Expanded * Community Tasks Complete * Enemypaedia Entry Complete (excluding Unique Monsters) * Collectopedia Entry Complete * Area Complete (Collectopaedia) * Completing a character's affinity growth

Conspirator MacNeth is a quest-exclusive Ardainian enemy in Torna ~ The Golden Country. He is fought during Duplicity at one of the abandoned houses at Hyber Village in the Aletta Region of the Kingdom of Torna.
Crackle Bullet is one of 's s in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected, and a clone of 's Thunder Bullet. It does two hits of and has a +25% against flying enemies.

The Corne Isl. Expedition are a duo of story exclusive bosses that are found on Corne Island at Erythia Sea. They are Testudos that can call for reinforcements through their Call Reinforcement Art, summoning several Agnian units, but they are not considered part of the Corne Isl. Expedition.
The Xenoblade Chronicles series of video games takes place in a system of distinct but connected universes.

Dark Daybreak (called Dark Dawn on the Revival disc and Xenogears Vinyl - SHINKAKU -, sometimes unofficially referred to as Light from the Netherworld) is Disc 1, Track 1 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack, Track 1 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack Revival Disc -the first and the last-, and Track 1 of the A-Side of the first disc of Xenogears Vinyl - SHINKAKU -. The melody at the start is used as a motif in Premonition, Awakening, and (from the Xenosaga Original Soundtrack) Opening. The melody at the end is based on a motif from Faraway Promise. It plays as the music in the opening cutscene, when the Eldridge is attacked and destroyed by Deus.

Deeds are key items in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. They can be bought from most lifestyle s, those that sell pouch items, after buying every other items in their stock, including key items, at least once, and are a single time purchase. Deeds provide the player with an array of beneficial effects, owner bonuses, which depend on the deed, such as the ability to hold more pouch items or a permanent increase to the player's running speed. Due to very few shops offering all their items for sale from the beginning, deeds usually require completing specific Merc Missions or s before they can be purchased. A few lifestyle shops that only sell one or two pouch items cannot have a deed up for sale. Payin

() is an enemy in Xenosaga I & II. It can be encountered in the Old Miltia City.

Dozing Off (Short Version) (called Doze (Short Version) on the Revival disc, sometimes unofficially referred to as Back to Sleep (Short Version)) is Disc 1, Track 10 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack and track 11 on the Xenogears Original Soundtrack Revival Disc -the first and the last-. It is one of the tracks playable in the Nortune jukebox, under the option 'Requiem'. It is a slightly shorter version of Dozing Off (Long Version) without the main melody line. The track is a jingle that plays when characters go to sleep, including: * After Fei has a flashback of Abel in the Blackmoon Forest. * The night before Margie's rescue in Bledavik.
Dive Bomber is an enemy in Xenogears. It is fought in the Blackmoon Forest.

Dual Moonblades are a in Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It is the main weapon of the , and the weapon used in Dominion Flower. This weapon can be upgraded by talking to Samon after completing Uniting the Seven Nopon. To upgrade, the following items are required: * 3 Round Origin Shards * 5 Toroidal Origin Shards * 3 Trigonal Origin Shards * 1 Hexagonal Origin Shard * 1 Square Origin Shard * 4 Rectangular Origin Shards * 4 Rhomboid Origin Shards The upgraded version of this weapon is called Sundancers.

Electric Discharge (, Lightning Element Launch) is one of 's discharge arts in Xenoblade Chronicles and Future Connected. It is a single bolt of electrical power that does high . While this art has a name and short description in the game data, they are not displayed; only the generic information is shown instead.
Dwarf is an enemy from Xenogears. It is fought in the Blackmoon Forest and on the world map outside Nisan and the Goliath Factory.
Edelweiss is an enemy in Xenogears. It is fought in the Mountain Cave.

Ein Rugel is a boss in Xenosaga Episode I - Der Wille zur Macht. It is a transformed version of the Blue Testament. It has an ability that blocks use of the button for all party members, preventing s. It also has an attack that inflicts Slow on all party members. After it loses its health it transforms into its second form, the Doppelwogel. Note that both Doppelwogel and Ein Rugel have rare items to steal, meaning that it's useful to steal from this form before moving on to the next.
The Eryth Sea Shop is a in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is located in Syrath Lighthouse at Eryth Sea and becomes available after the party leave Alcamoth for Prison Island.

The following is a list of the music tracks in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and Torna ~ The Golden Country that are counted as 'Environment' as opposed to 'Game BGM' in the sound settings; as such, they do not override the in-game background music. All are apparently played in-universe, and none have been released on any soundtrack or sound selection. As such, not much is known about any of the following tracks, including their composers.

Escape is Disc 2, Track 19 on the Xenosaga Original Soundtrack, Disc 1, Track 16 on the album, and Track 2 on the DigiCube original Xenosaga music CD. It plays in the cutscene when the Elsa enters Second Miltia's atmosphere. It is interrupted by Kokoro o Tozashita Shôjo when KOS-MOS and chaos briefly talk during this scene, and resumes when KOS-MOS exits the aft hatch of the Elsa.
Ether Awareness is the first skill in 's Reliability skill branch. It gives her +25 .

Fast Travel is a gameplay mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It allows the player to teleport to any previously-discovered or FN Site while not in battle, thus saving time not having to walk there manually. In the Wii U version, fast travel was done by tapping on a hexagon with a discovered landmark or and then pressing the "Fast Travel" button. In the , fast travel is done by opening the map and clicking on a landmark or unlocked FN Site. When the player has a Skell and has dismounted, it is possible to open the pause menu, select "Party", and then "Return to Skell" in order to fast travel to it. This uses both Arts while only going through the animation of the Class Art, and comes with a variety of other beneficial effects. The Life Recycling Act, also known as the Life Recycling Law is a law in the Xenosaga series. It was drafted in T.C. 4590 by the Galaxy Federation and approved in T.C. 4591. The term "Life Recycling Variant" describes anyone who had their biological components modified as a result of this law. Due to the many controversies surrounding it, it was eventually repealed in T.C. 4754. The Species Preservation Act was later enacted to counter its harmful effects.

Most party-member equipment in Xenoblade Chronicles X is produced in-universe by one of the Arms Manufacturers, which determines aspects such as its Battle Traits. However, this does not apply to all equipment; some have their manufacture given as "unknown". This article contains a list of such equipment.

The Lifehold Database Chamber is a cutscene-exclusive area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located inside the Lifehold Core and stores all the consciousnesses and memories of the humans of the White Whale. During the inspection at the end of , Elma discovers that the entire database chamber was flooded and destroyed and concludes that it had been caused by the crash landing of the White Whale on Mira. It is unknown why the people of NLA are still alive.

Melee Attack is a stat for both ground and Skell units in Xenoblade Chronicles X that represents a combatant's melee attack power. The Miltian Conflict is an event in the Xenosaga series and the final battle of the Zoar Incident that occurred on Miltia in the year T.C. 4753. It is the reason why the planet Miltia was sealed and resulted in Gnosis attacks becoming frequent. Various news media across the U.M.N. calls the incident an act of terrorism.
The Miltian Hierocracy was an independent theocratic nation in the Xenosaga series. It is the regime that preceded the Miltian Republic on the planet Miltia.

The Miltian Republic, also known as the Miltian Autonomous State, was a regime in the Xenosaga series that oversaw the Miltian star system. It was the government system that succeeded the Miltian Hierocracy and preceded the Theocratic Government of Miltia.
Moonbeam Contract is an unused contract key item in Xenoblade Chronicles 2.

The music is primarily made with a combination of recorded instruments and electronic instruments, and is in general of significantly lower audio quality than the soundtracks of the mainline Xenosaga games. Since the 3DS is a console made to take it wherever the user want, it can be folded to maximize the portability. The console features two cameras (front and back), one microphone, gyroscope and a stylus. On , the 3DS systems received a major system update that added compatibility with Miiverse, a social media created by Nintendo. The Nopon trade guilds, sometimes capitalized as Nopon Trade Guild, are a set of eleven guilds dedicated to trading and ran by the Nopon. These guilds serve as a neutral meeting ground for Alrest's nations. As such, the guilds are locations that can act as a midway point for travels between Titans, where goods can be sold or auctioned off, where money can be lent or salvaging can be practiced. Not every guild is equal in power, with the weakest and strongest of them varying between time periods.

The Old City is an area in Future Redeemed. It is only used in the battle against and in cutscenes, meaning that it cannot be explored.

The Nopwatch is a mechanic in the Archsage's Gauntlet mode of Xenoblade Chronicles 3. It is a timer which slowly ticks down during fights, and if it reaches zero, the party's combat capabilities are greatly reduced. This prevents the player from trying to win based on stalling, turtling, or other slow strategies.
